scenarios.title: Measure the busy interval, not the boot average
scenarios.summary: Compare actual CPU windows and runnable work before publishing a measured report.
scenarios.objective: Use the boot-a recording to compare every one-second interval wholly inside 3000–5000 ms. Report the highest and lowest executing-work percentages and the largest runnable-process reading from those interval rows. Executing work is the displayed us + sy + gu total. Attach an actual interval row to each claim; do not use the first since-boot row. Enter whole numbers with the units already shown. Run commands against the supplied recording, then choose Check report. Equivalent supported commands and tied eligible intervals are valid.
steps: Investigate the supplied recording, attach measured evidence and check the complete report.
scenarios.explanation: Choose boot-a at 3.000 s and run vmstat 1 3. Row 2 is 3000–4000 ms: us 50 + sy 30 + gu 0 = 80% executing work, with r 4. Row 3 is 4000–5000 ms: us 10 + sy 10 + gu 0 = 20%. Attach Row 2 to the highest-work and largest-runnable claims and Row 3 to the lowest-work claim; enter 80,4 and 20 in the matching fields and Check report. The first since-boot row is not an eligible interval. Equivalent supported commands pass.
hints: Choose the requested boot and time before running a finite command. Row 1 of vmstat is a boot average, not an interval.
Use the units beside each report field. Attach a result row, then type the measured value; the fields do not copy solved answers automatically.
For a peak/trough compare every eligible interval. For MemAvailable use the final virtual meminfo. Check each report row’s evidence caption before checking.
scenarios.simplifications: Finite replay of supplied synthetic Linux observations, not a live machine. Only disclosed vmstat forms and the eight-field virtual meminfo are supported. No actual time wait, host /proc read, process, swap, service, disk or network operation. Unknown syntax, missing intervals, mixed sources and decreasing counters fail honestly. Rounded displayed percentages can sum slightly above or below 100. This measures recorded facts; it does not identify a hardware bottleneck, prove pressure or implement the wider LPIC-2 monitoring-tool set. Sources checked 2026-11-11; procps/kernel latest URLs are mutable.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the specific report-row feedback. Check source boot, whether the row is since boot or an interval, and the labeled units before changing a value.

scenarios.title: Separate allocated swap from current paging
scenarios.summary: Use activity rates and available memory to avoid diagnosing pressure from a footprint alone.
scenarios.objective: Inspect paging-a over 60000–63000 ms. Find the highest and lowest one-second swap-out rates, using actual interval rows as evidence. At 63000 ms, report allocated swap and MemAvailable. Use the final snapshot; allocated swap is SwapTotal minus SwapFree, while MemAvailable is supplied directly. Enter whole KiB/s or KiB as labeled, attach the corresponding evidence and choose Check report. Any tied minimum-rate interval is valid. The task asks for measured facts, not an unsupported diagnosis.
steps: Investigate the supplied recording, attach measured evidence and check the complete report.
scenarios.explanation: Choose paging-a at 60.000 s and run vmstat 1 4. The first interval so is 1024 KiB/s; the next two are 0. Attach those interval rows to the highest/lowest swap-out claims. At 63.000 s, run cat /proc/meminfo: SwapTotal 4194304 minus SwapFree 1048576 gives 3145728 KiB allocated, while MemAvailable is 2097152 KiB. Attach the snapshot to those two claims and enter the values. Allocated swap has remained present while current transfer activity stopped; this alone is not a complete pressure diagnosis.
hints: Choose the requested boot and time before running a finite command. Row 1 of vmstat is a boot average, not an interval.
Use the units beside each report field. Attach a result row, then type the measured value; the fields do not copy solved answers automatically.
For allocated swap subtract SwapFree from SwapTotal. For activity compare interval so, including zero rates; those quantities have different units.

scenarios.title: Publish a coherent post-restart measurement handover
scenarios.summary: Recover useful observations without joining incompatible boots or reporting the wrong period.
scenarios.objective: Report only handover-new, using all eligible one-second intervals inside 1000–5000 ms. Find the highest executing-work percentage and the highest block-output rate. Report MemAvailable at the final 5000 ms post-restart snapshot. Attach actual measurements for all three claims; do not mix handover-old averages or rows into the report. Use the supported terminal and report controls, then Check report. You may avoid an incompatible request or recover after its diagnostic. A failed command is never usable evidence.
steps: Investigate the supplied recording, attach measured evidence and check the complete report.
scenarios.explanation: Choose handover-new at 1.000 s and run vmstat 1 5. Row 2 describes 1000–2000 ms and has 95% executing work and 2048 KiB/s block output, the highest eligible displayed readings. Attach that interval to both peak claims. At handover-new 5.000 s, run cat /proc/meminfo and attach its snapshot for MemAvailable 1572864 KiB. Check report. Old-boot or since-boot activity rows cannot establish the requested post-restart peaks; other supported finite requests measuring these facts are valid.
hints: Choose the requested boot and time before running a finite command. Row 1 of vmstat is a boot average, not an interval.
Use the units beside each report field. Attach a result row, then type the measured value; the fields do not copy solved answers automatically.
Start on handover-new at 1.000 s. The compatible finite request produces one boot-average row and four interval rows; the final snapshot is at 5.000 s.
